raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

CPU wheels expose Triton as a GitHub URL dependency, which uv rejects when resolving vLLM from an index and which prevents offline wheelhouse installation. Publish the same CPU Triton build as an indexed dependency and retain its exact version and platform conditions. Fixes #62322.

## Claims

- CPU wheel metadata uses `triton==3.8.0+cpu` with the original Python/architecture markers.
- The x86 CPU upload stages both supported Python wheels after verifying their SHA256 pins. Commit, nightly and release indices include the dependency; download or checksum failures stop publication.
- Installation docs select CPU Triton explicitly with `--find-links` when using `uv --torch-backend cpu`, and provide an offline wheelhouse workflow.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tools/test_cpu_wheel_distribution.py -q
.venv/bin/python tests/standalone_tests/test_precompiled_wheel.py
.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files setup.py requirements/cpu.txt .buildkite/scripts/stage-cpu-triton-wheels.sh .buildkite/scripts/upload-nightly-wheels.sh .buildkite/scripts/generate-nightly-index.py tests/standalone_tests/test_precompiled_wheel.py tests/tools/test_cpu_wheel_distribution.py .buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml docs/getting_started/installation/cpu.x86.inc.md
```

11 distribution tests and 11 setup tests passed. All applicable hooks, including pip-compile-cpu, ShellCheck, mypy and Buildkite test tethering, passed. New tests run in the existing CPU suite.

Additional Linux x86_64/Python 3.12 validation used the actual `0.32.0+cpu` release wheel, changing only its Triton Requires-Dist entries to those generated by setup.py and regenerating RECORD. All 3306 other archive members were verified identical. Original wheel: named-index resolution fails on the transitive URL. Changed wheel with the documented options: 152 packages resolve, download and install into a fresh environment using `--offline --no-index --find-links`; `uv pip check` passes. Imports of installed vLLM/LLM/SamplingParams/native extension and real Triton CPU JIT vector addition passed. S3 writes were replayed locally; no production upload was performed.

## Details

Filtering official wheel indices by the vLLM version discards Triton's independent version, so the release filter must preserve CPU Triton just as it preserves the XPU shim. Uploading dependencies before the vLLM wheel prevents a failed download/checksum from exposing a new wheel without its dependency.

`--torch-backend cpu` also restricts Triton to the PyTorch index. Hosting the CPU build alone therefore does not fix the existing uv command; `--find-links` supplies CPU candidates while retaining `first-index` selection for vLLM and the CPU Torch backend. Ordinary `triton==3.8.0` was not substituted for the CPU artifact.

Duplicate checks found no open PR implementing #62322 or the CPU wheel dependency publication fix. This changes packaging and distribution, with no model-output or performance claim. Existing published wheels are not rewritten; the normal release pipeline must publish new wheels and indices after merging.

AI assistance from OpenAI Codex was used during development.

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+
+set -euo pipefail
+
+urls=$(sed -n 's/^triton @ \([^ ;]*\).*/\1/p' requirements/cpu.txt)
+if [[ -z "$urls" ]]; then
+    echo "No Triton CPU wheels found in requirements/cpu.txt" >&2
+    exit 1
+fi
+
+work_dir=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'rm -rf "$work_dir"' EXIT
+
+while IFS= read -r url; do
+    digest="${url##*#sha256=}"
+    if [[ ! "$digest" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]]; then
+        echo "Triton CPU wheel must have a SHA256 pin: $url" >&2
+        exit 1
+    fi
+    filename="${url%%#*}"
+    filename="${filename##*/}"
+    curl --fail --location --retry 3 --output "$work_dir/$filename" "$url"
+    printf '%s  %s\n' "$digest" "$work_dir/$filename" | sha256sum --check -
+done <<< "$urls"
+
+# Verify every supported Python wheel before publishing any of them.
+aws s3 cp --recursive "$work_dir/" "s3://vllm-wheels/${BUILDKITE_COMMIT:?}/"

 To install the wheel built from the latest main branch:
 
 ```bash
-uv pip install vllm --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/nightly/cpu --index-strategy first-index --torch-backend cpu
+uv pip install vllm --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/nightly/cpu \

+The `--find-links` option supplies Triton CPU wheels from the vLLM index;
+`--torch-backend cpu` otherwise restricts Triton to the PyTorch index.
+
 #### Install specific revisions
 
 If you want to access the wheels for previous commits (e.g. to bisect the behavior change, performance regression), you can specify the commit hash in the URL:
 
 ```bash
 export VLLM_COMMIT=730bd35378bf2a5b56b6d3a45be28b3092d26519 # use full commit hash from the main branch
-uv pip install vllm --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/${VLLM_COMMIT}/cpu --index-strategy first-index --torch-backend cpu

+    --find-links https://wheels.vllm.ai/${VLLM_COMMIT}/cpu/triton/ \
+    --index-strategy first-index --torch-backend cpu
+```
+
+#### Install without internet access
+
+On a connected machine with the same OS, architecture and Python version as the
+target, download the release wheel and all dependencies:
+
+```bash
+uvx pip download "vllm==${VLLM_VERSION}+cpu" --only-binary=:all: --dest wheelhouse \
+    --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/${VLLM_VERSION}/cpu \
+    --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu
+```
+
+Transfer `wheelhouse` to the target, then install without accessing any index:
+
+```bash
+uv pip install "vllm==${VLLM_VERSION}+cpu" --offline --no-index --find-links wheelhouse
 ```

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+
+import hashlib
+import json
+import os
+import subprocess
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+from urllib.parse import unquote
+
+import pytest
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
+TRITON_WHEELS = [
+    f"triton-3.8.0+cpu-{tag}-manylinux_2_27_x86_64.manylinux_2_28_x86_64.whl"
+    for tag in ("cp311-cp311", "cp312-abi3")
+]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("version", ["a" * 40, "0.32.0", "0.32.0rc1"])
+def test_cpu_dependency_remains_in_commit_and_release_indices(tmp_path, version):
+    """Release filtering must not discard the CPU wheel's dependency."""
+    commit_dir = tmp_path / ("a" * 40)
+    index_dir = tmp_path / version
+    vllm_wheel = "vllm-0.32.0+cpu-cp38-abi3-manylinux_2_34_x86_64.whl"
+    xpu_wheel = "triton-3.8.0+xpu-py3-none-any.whl"
+    objects = tmp_path / "objects.json"
+    objects.write_text(
+        json.dumps(
+            {
+                "Contents": [
+                    {"Key": f"{commit_dir.name}/{name}"}
+                    for name in [vllm_wheel, xpu_wheel, *TRITON_WHEELS]
+                ]
+            }
+        )
+    )
+    subprocess.run(
+        [
+            sys.executable,
+            str(ROOT / ".buildkite/scripts/generate-nightly-index.py"),
+            "--version",
+            version,
+            "--wheel-dir",
+            commit_dir.name,
+            "--current-objects",
+            str(objects),
+            "--output-dir",
+            str(index_dir),
+        ],
+        check=True,
+        capture_output=True,
+        text=True,
+    )
+    links = unquote((index_dir / "cpu/triton/index.html").read_text())
+    metadata = json.loads((index_dir / "cpu/triton/metadata.json").read_text())
+    assert {entry["filename"] for entry in metadata} == set(TRITON_WHEELS)
+    for wheel in TRITON_WHEELS:
+        assert f'/{wheel}"' in links
+    assert xpu_wheel not in links
+    assert (index_dir / "xpu/triton/index.html").exists()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("failure", [None, "checksum", "http", "missing-pin"])
+def test_stage_all_python_wheels_only_after_verifying_downloads(tmp_path, failure):
+    """A failure on the second wheel must prevent every S3 upload."""
+    payload = b"fixture wheel bytes"
+    digest = hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest()
+    requirements = tmp_path / "requirements"
+    requirements.mkdir()
+    urls = []
+    for i, wheel in enumerate(TRITON_WHEELS):
+        checksum = "0" * 64 if i == 1 and failure == "checksum" else digest
+        fragment = "" if i == 1 and failure == "missing-pin" else f"#sha256={checksum}"
+        urls.append(f"triton @ https://github.com/fixture/{wheel}{fragment}")
+    (requirements / "cpu.txt").write_text("\n".join(urls))
+    bin_dir = tmp_path / "bin"
+    bin_dir.mkdir()
+    curl = bin_dir / "curl"
+    curl.write_text(
+        f"#!{sys.executable}\n"
+        "import os, sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n"
+        "if os.environ['FAILURE'] == 'http' and 'cp312' in sys.argv[-1]:\n"
+        "    sys.exit(22)\n"
+        f"Path(sys.argv[sys.argv.index('--output') + 1]).write_bytes({payload!r})\n"
+    )
+    aws = bin_dir / "aws"
+    aws.write_text(
+        f"#!{sys.executable}\n"
+        "import json, sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n"
+        "assert sys.argv[1:4] == ['s3', 'cp', '--recursive']\n"
+        "Path('uploads.json').write_text(json.dumps({\n"
+        "    'files': sorted(p.name for p in Path(sys.argv[4]).iterdir()),\n"
+        "    'target': sys.argv[5]}))\n"
+    )
+    curl.chmod(0o755)
+    aws.chmod(0o755)
+    result = subprocess.run(
+        ["bash", str(ROOT / ".buildkite/scripts/stage-cpu-triton-wheels.sh")],
+        cwd=tmp_path,
+        env={
+            **os.environ,
+            "PATH": f"{bin_dir}:{os.environ['PATH']}",
+            "BUILDKITE_COMMIT": "a" * 40,
+            "FAILURE": failure or "",
+        },
+        capture_output=True,
+        text=True,
+        timeout=15,
+    )
+    uploads = tmp_path / "uploads.json"
+    if failure:
+        assert result.returncode != 0
+        assert not uploads.exists()
+    else:
+        assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr
+        assert json.loads(uploads.read_text()) == {
+            "files": sorted(TRITON_WHEELS),
+            "target": f"s3://vllm-wheels/{'a' * 40}/",
+        }
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "version,arch,needs_triton",
+    [
+        ("0.32.0+cpu", "x86_64", True),
+        ("0.32.1.dev1+gabcdef.cpu", "x86_64", True),
+        ("0.32.0+cpu", "aarch64", False),
+        ("0.32.0", "x86_64", False),
+    ],
+)
+def test_uploader_stages_dependency_before_x86_cpu_wheel(
+    tmp_path, version, arch, needs_triton
+):
+    """Release and nightly builds must both publish the dependency first."""
+    import zipfile
+
+    dist = tmp_path / "artifacts/dist"
+    dist.mkdir(parents=True)
+    wheel = dist / f"vllm-{version}-cp38-abi3-manylinux_2_34_{arch}.whl"
+    with zipfile.ZipFile(wheel, "w") as archive:
+        archive.writestr("vllm.dist-info/METADATA", f"Version: {version}\n")
+    scripts = tmp_path / ".buildkite/scripts"
+    scripts.mkdir(parents=True)
+    (scripts / "lib").symlink_to(ROOT / ".buildkite/scripts/lib")
+    # The stage command's downloads and checksum validation are exercised above.
+    (scripts / "stage-cpu-triton-wheels.sh").write_text("echo dependency >> calls\n")
+    bin_dir = tmp_path / "bin"
+    bin_dir.mkdir()
+    # Exercise the uploader's real control flow; avoid launching auditwheel Docker.
+    docker = bin_dir / "docker"
+    docker.write_text(
+        "#!/bin/bash\n"
+        'case "$1" in\n'
+        "  run) echo fixture-container ;;\n"
+        '  exec) [[ "${*: -1}" == *.whl ]] && echo "${*: -1}"; exit 0 ;;\n'
+        "esac\n"
+    )
+    aws = bin_dir / "aws"
+    aws.write_text("#!/bin/sh\necho vllm >> calls\n")
+    unzip = bin_dir / "unzip"
+    unzip.write_text(
+        f"#!{sys.executable}\n"
+        "import sys, zipfile\n"
+        "with zipfile.ZipFile(sys.argv[2]) as archive:\n"
+        "    path = next(n for n in archive.namelist() if n.endswith('/METADATA'))\n"
+        "    sys.stdout.write(archive.read(path).decode())\n"
+    )
+    docker.chmod(0o755)
+    aws.chmod(0o755)
+    unzip.chmod(0o755)
+    result = subprocess.run(
+        ["bash", str(ROOT / ".buildkite/scripts/upload-nightly-wheels.sh")],
+        cwd=tmp_path,
+        env={
+            **os.environ,
+            "PATH": f"{bin_dir}:{os.environ['PATH']}",
+            "BUILDKITE_COMMIT": "a" * 40,
+            "VLLM_WHEEL_PLATFORM": "linux",
+        },
+        capture_output=True,
+        text=True,
+        timeout=15,
+    )
+    assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr
+    expected = ["dependency", "vllm"] if needs_triton else ["vllm"]
+    assert (tmp_path / "calls").read_text().splitlines() == expected
